shortDescription: Stacks up to seven playable levels (three sky, surface, three underground) into one banded RimWorld map, joined through the engine's own region system so pathing, hauling and cross-level combat work without patching reachability.
body:
## What this mod is

RimWorld is flat. As above, So below II stacks up to seven playable levels into a single map: up to three sky levels, the surface, and up to three underground. They are **bands of one real map**, joined through the engine's own region system, so reachability, pathfinding and region code are never patched — the game just finds a path. Harmony is the only hard dependency.

The level plan (how many levels above/below, and level size) is chosen per colony at colony start, sharing one cell budget. Mod settings hold the default plan: `multiLevel = true`, `upperLevels = 1`, `lowerLevels = 1`. The generated layout is scribed on `ABBandMap`, so existing saves never depend on the settings values.

## Major systems

- **Traversal** — ladders (1 cell), staircases (2×2), grand staircases (3×3), elevators (2×2, connecting every level in a shaft). Placement validation refuses spots that would jam.
- **Cross-level combat** — a pawn can shoot anything visible through a real opening, in both directions; turrets and raider AI acquire across levels; mortars ignore the rule; misses resolve on the target's level.
- **Arrivals** — raiders, visitors, traders and animals may arrive/leave via other levels, per-category toggles. Upper on, lower off by default. Anyone who can arrive can also leave (never a trap).
- **Sky levels** — real summit terrain above mountains; roofing a room makes its rooftop walkable/buildable above.
- **Underground levels** — solid mineable rock, ore density ~1.5× per level down. With Biomes! Caverns, generates as a living cave system instead.
- **See-below rendering** — live view of the actual surface from sky levels using the game's own materials, with tunable depth falloff.
- **Climate by altitude** — per-level temperature offset and wind, baked at colony creation. Three presets (Gentle / Standard / Alpine).
- **Utility columns** — power, pipe, climate and data columns merge the networks of the two levels they join. Pipe networks are detected at runtime rather than hard-coded, so unpatched pipe mods work.
- **Kill switches** — each subsystem logs once, disables itself and names what it was doing on error (`ABGuard`), so a failure never takes down the rest of the mod or vanilla.

## Research progression

Two tiers, and the concrete buildables carry their own `researchPrerequisites` rather than inheriting from the abstract bases (`AB_ColumnBase` / `AB_WallRiserBase`) — this is deliberate, so the Pipe variants can be gated separately from the other three.

| Project | Cost | Tech | Prerequisite |
|---|---|---|---|
| `AB2_Stairs` | 400 | Neolithic | `VFET_Construction` *(MayRequire VFE Tribals)* |
| `AB2_Ladders` | 300 | Neolithic | `VFET_Construction` *(MayRequire VFE Tribals)* |
| `AB2_PipeColumns` | 300 | Medieval | `Plumbing` *(MayRequire Dubs Bad Hygiene)* |
| `AB2_TransferColumns` | 1200 | Industrial | `Fabrication` (vanilla) |
| `AB2_ElevatorTech` | — | — | `AB2_Stairs` |

Gating map for the 8 concrete buildables: Power / Climate / Data columns and their wall risers → `AB2_TransferColumns`; Pipe column and Pipe wall riser → `AB2_PipeColumns`.

The per-network connect toggles independently respect each host mod's own research (`Building_ABColumn.GetGizmos` → `AB2_ColumnNeedsResearch`), so unlocking a column does not bypass a network's own gate.

## Compatibility

Optional, all runtime-detected: Biomes! Caverns, Combat Extended (experimental), VE pipe framework, Dubs Bad Hygiene, Rimefeller, Rimatomics, RimIOT, Eccentric Tech Defense Grid, VFE, Better Mountains, Medieval Overhaul, Map Preview, Dubs Mint Minimap, Geological Landforms, Vanilla Landmarks Expanded. Hard-incompatible with the original As above So below, MultiFloors, Z-Levels and Strata.

## Dev tooling

~65 debug actions under the **"As above"** category. Documented order of use: `AB2: band info` first (it reports `NO WORMHOLE PAIRS REGISTERED`, the fastest way to see a map has no stairs yet), then `AB2: why can't this pawn shoot that` for a specific failure, then `AB2: combat report` for counters. Also stress spawners, bisect toggles for isolating render layers, and probes for pathing/mining/water/roof.

## Assets

`ABTex.cs` loads `UI/AB_ViewLevelUp` and `UI/AB_ViewLevelDown` via `ContentFinder` for the view-level gizmo; both are declared in `.circinus/cs-assets.json`.
